title: A High Level Approach to Co-Designing 3D ICs
problem: 3D ICs suffer from timing closure challenges when architecture and physical design are optimized separately. Traditional sequential approaches (binding then placement) miss optimization opportunities for 3D-specific layout constraints.
motivation: 3D ICs offer increased logic density and reduced routing congestion over 2D designs, making timing closure improvements critical to realizing these benefits.
method: The approach combines two design steps that are usually done separately, one after the other. It uses high-level synthesis (automatic conversion of high-level code-like specifications into hardware designs) to explore architectural choices while simultaneously optimizing the physical placement of large components within a 3D-stacked chip structure. Both steps iterate together—each iteration refines the architecture based on physical layout constraints and refines component placement based on architectural changes—until reaching an optimal design.
key_novelty: The key contribution is combining 3D IC architecture design and physical component placement into one simultaneous optimization process, rather than treating them as separate sequential steps.
contributions: Unified co-design methodology combining HLS and 3D IC macro placement
62% average TNS reduction for 2D ICs versus traditional binding and placement
92% average TNS reduction for 3D ICs versus traditional binding and placement
Increased optimization flexibility through higher-level design abstraction
primary_theme: 3D IC timing optimization via HLS co-design
